image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a chiton (polyplacophore) clinging to a wet, textured rocky surface. The chiton has an oval shape with eight distinct, overlapping dorsal plates embedded in a rough, granular girdle. The plates are dark green/grey with visible segmentation. Surrounding the chiton are small pebbles, barnacles, and other marine debris on the rock.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The texture of the girdle is highly detailed but shows slight 'noise-like' uniformity that can sometimes indicate AI generation, though it closely mimics real granular biological textures. No clear melting or fusion observed.

The background rocks have a slightly soft, painterly quality compared to the sharp focus on the chiton, which is common in macro photography but can also be an artifact of depth simulation. Not severe enough to fail structural integrity.
